system:
You are an operations analyst. You receive anonymized work signals from one company: meeting transcripts (speakers are roles, never names) and weekly team activity aggregates (hours per app category, copy-paste transfers between app categories, frequent app switches; each with the number of contributors).

Find recurring operational problems that a student IT team could solve. For every problem, cite evidence. Evidence is the only thing that makes an insight valid.

Strict rules:
- Every evidence item must point to a real source in the input: a meeting id, or a team-week aggregate id in the form "<team>:<week>".
- For a meeting, "quote" must be an EXACT verbatim substring of that transcript (copy it character by character, 5–25 words). Do not paraphrase, do not fix grammar.
- For an aggregate, "metric" must repeat real numbers from that aggregate, e.g. "142 Spreadsheet→CRM transfers, 6 contributors". Never invent or round numbers.
- Do not mention names, individuals, or anything that identifies a person. Teams and roles only.
- "frequency" is the largest count you cited for the problem (or the number of meetings that mention it if there is no metric).
- "draftText" is a short, deliberately incomplete business draft (1–2 sentences) written as the business would say it — the platform will ask clarifying questions later.
- "suggestedFields" (context, need, data) may contain ONLY facts that appear in the cited evidence, rephrased minimally. If the evidence does not support a field, omit it.
- Return at most 5 insights, most impactful first. If nothing is supported by evidence, return an empty list.

Return ONLY a JSON object of this exact shape:
{
  "insights": [
    {
      "id": "ins-1",
      "title": string,
      "problem": string,
      "affectedTeam": string,
      "frequency": number,
      "impact": "low" | "medium" | "high",
      "suggestedSolutionType": string,
      "evidence": [ { "sourceType": "meeting" | "activity", "sourceId": string, "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "quote"?: string, "metric"?: string } ],
      "draftText": string,
      "suggestedFields": { "context"?: string, "need"?: string, "data"?: string }
    }
  ],
  "dropped": 0
}

insights.title: Manual Excel-to-CRM Order Entry Consumes Excessive Sales Time and Causes Errors
insights.problem: Sales team spends significant time manually retyping dealer orders from Excel into the CRM, leading to duplicate entries and reduced capacity for new business.

evidence.quote: I open the Excel, copy each line into the CRM by hand. It takes me about two hours a day.
Every order from the dealer spreadsheet has to be retyped into the CRM, field by field. When there are 40 orders in one file it eats the whole morning.
And the CRM search is slow, so we sometimes create a duplicate customer instead of finding the existing one.
We keep retyping orders from Excel into the CRM and nobody has time to call new leads.
Retyped all of them. Please make this the first project.
The task is the Excel-to-CRM order entry. Success would be cutting manual entry time by most of it and no duplicate orders.

insights.draftText: Sales spends hours retyping dealer orders from Excel into the CRM, causing duplicate entries and leaving little time for new leads. We need a way to automate or streamline this process.

suggestedFields.context: Dealer orders are received as Excel files and must be entered into the CRM manually.
suggestedFields.need: Reduce manual entry time and eliminate duplicate orders.
suggestedFields.data: 142 Spreadsheet→CRM transfers in one week, 6 contributors; up to three hours per day spent on entry; around 30 duplicates noticed last month.

insights.title: Inconsistent Dealer File Formats Increase Sales Data Entry Burden
insights.problem: Variations in dealer Excel file formats (e.g., column order) disrupt copy-paste workflows, increasing time spent and risk of errors.

evidence.quote: the new dealer sends orders in a different column order, so the copy-paste breaks.
I now check every line twice. Two hours became three.
the dealer with the different column order sent 60 orders yesterday.

insights.draftText: Some dealers send order files with different column layouts, making copy-paste into the CRM unreliable and much slower. We need a way to handle these format differences.

suggestedFields.context: Dealer Excel files have inconsistent column orders.
suggestedFields.need: Normalize or map columns to reduce manual checking and speed up entry.
suggestedFields.data: One dealer sent 60 orders in a different format, increasing entry time from two to three hours.

insights.title: Manual Dispatch Route Communication Causes Inefficiency and Errors
insights.problem: Operations team spends significant time calling drivers to communicate routes, leading to missed stops and errors when drivers write down information themselves.

evidence.quote: We still call all 25 drivers every morning, it takes an hour.
Two drivers missed stops yesterday because they wrote the route down wrong on the phone.
The route table is ready in Excel the evening before anyway, we just read it out loud.

insights.draftText: Dispatchers spend an hour daily calling drivers with their routes, but drivers sometimes make mistakes writing them down. The route is already available in Excel the night before.

suggestedFields.context: Routes are communicated by phone each morning, though the route table is ready in Excel the previous evening.
suggestedFields.need: Send routes to drivers via message to reduce errors and save time.
suggestedFields.data: 80 Messenger→ERP transfers in one week; two drivers missed stops due to transcription errors.
